title: Understanding the Model
text:
Wesley's model is a linear regression model with transformations applied to the features. The model is given by:

\( \hat{y}_i=\hat{	heta}_0+\hat{	heta}_1(x_{i1})**{3}+\hat{	heta}_{2}\log(x_{i2}) \)

This means that the model is linear in the parameters \( \hat{	heta}_0, \hat{	heta}_1, \hat{	heta}_2 \), but not necessarily in the features.

title: Span of X
text: The span of a matrix \( X \) refers to all possible linear combinations of its columns. For the vector of outcomes \( Y \) to be in the span of \( X \), it means that \( Y \) can be expressed as a linear combination of the columns of \( X \).

title: Unique Optimal Solution
text: A unique optimal solution in the context of OLS implies that the matrix \( $$X^{TX}$$ \) is invertible. This is typically the case when the columns of \( X \) are linearly independent.

title: Checking Linear Independence
text: Given that Wesley has $$30$$ unique data points and $$2$$ features, can we assume that the columns of \( X \) are linearly independent?

title: Conclusion on the Span
text: Since the columns of \( X \) are linearly independent, \( $$X^{TX}$$ \) is invertible, and thus \( Y \) is in the span of \( X \).
